lesson_yaml:
schema: cairn/lesson/v0.1
id: java-xwiki-saving-document-without-checksavingdocument
title: XWiki document saved via saveDocument without checkSavingDocument after setting author
summary: Code sets the document author to the current user and calls XWiki#saveDocument directly, without
  first calling checkSavingDocument. Skipping that check bypasses the content-author and required-rights
  verification that XWiki performs when a user saves a document. A user could therefore persist changes
  that they are not entitled to make, or have content saved with an inappropriate author.
cwe:
- CWE-862
severity: medium
confidence: medium
languages:
- java
source:
  kind: fix-commit
  ref: 448b0f074cc6711410eb2647c4740454c92d1626
  vulnerable_ref: 448b0f074cc6711410eb2647c4740454c92d1626^
  patched_ref: 448b0f074cc6711410eb2647c4740454c92d1626
  repository: https://github.com/xwiki/xwiki-platform
rule:
  message: 'Document is saved with saveDocument() after the author is set, but XWiki#checkSavingDocument()
    is not

    called first. Call checkSavingDocument(userReference, document, comment, true, xcontext) before saving.

    '
  patterns:
  - pattern: $XC.getWiki().saveDocument($DOC, $COMMENT, $MINOR, $XC);
  - pattern-inside: "$RET $METHOD(...) {\n  ...\n  $DOC.setAuthorReference(...);\n  ...\n}\n"
  - pattern-not-inside: "$RET $METHOD(...) {\n  ...\n  $XC.getWiki().checkSavingDocument(...);\n  ...\n\
      }\n"

sibling_hits.reason: TagPlugin sets the author to the current user and saves directly without checkSavingDocument, so a user could persist a tag change they may not be entitled to make.
Removing a tag follows the same pattern: the author is set to the current user and the document is saved without checkSavingDocument.
Renaming a tag across documents sets the author and calls saveDocument directly, with no checkSavingDocument verification.
Legacy backlink-rename code sets the author and saves without checkSavingDocument, but the callers and any rights checks on the backlink documents are not visible here.
DefaultDocumentAccessBridge is an internal trusted bridge component that deliberately does not do user-level rights checks, so this is not the user-facing save path the lesson is about.
